source.text: לַמְנַצֵּ֤חַ׀עַל־י֬וֹנַת אֵ֣לֶם רְ֭חֹקִים לְדָוִ֣ד מִכְתָּ֑ם בֶּֽאֱחֹ֨ז אֹת֖וֹ פְלִשְׁתִּ֣ים בְּגַֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: For the director, on yonath elem rechokim, of David, a miktam, when seized him [the] Philistines in Gath.

en.L: For the director: on yonath elem rechokim. Of David. A miktam, when the Philistines seized him in Gath.
en.B: For the music director. On yonath elem rechokim. Of David. A miktam, when the Philistines seized him in Gath.
en.R: For the leader of the music. To the tune "A Silent Dove Far Away". A song by David, from the time when the Philistines captured him in Gath.

decisions.choice: The title is verse 1
decisions.reason: The title is part of the Hebrew text and is counted as verse 1, so the verse numbers here are one higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: the director: the one who leads the music
decisions.reason: As in 4:1, probably the leader of the temple music.

decisions.choice: yonath elem rechokim: "a silent dove of far-off places", probably a tune
alternatives: the dove of the distant oaks
decisions.reason: The words mean something like "a dove of silence, of distant ones"; with other vowels, "a dove of the distant oaks". It is probably the name of a tune. Its exact sense is lost; compare the dove of 55:7.

decisions.choice: miktam: a kind of psalm whose meaning is unknown
decisions.reason: As in 16:1. The word (miktam) heads Psalms 16 and 56-60. Its meaning is lost; the ancient Greek translation took it as an inscription on a stone, and others link it to a word for gold.

decisions.choice: David in Gath: 1 Samuel 21
decisions.reason: Fleeing from Saul, David went to Achish, king of the Philistine city of Gath, and when he was recognized he escaped by pretending to be mad (1 Samuel 21). The title of Psalm 34 refers to the same event.

decisions.choice: To the tune "A Silent Dove Far Away"
decisions.reason: Readable translates the words and takes them as a tune name (m3).

decisions.choice: A song
decisions.reason: Its meaning is unknown; Readable says only that it is a song.

source.text: חָנֵּ֣נִי אֱ֭לֹהִים כִּֽי־שְׁאָפַ֣נִי אֱנ֑וֹשׁ כָּל־הַ֝יּ֗וֹם לֹחֵ֥ם יִלְחָצֵֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: Be gracious to me, God, for has trampled on me a mortal; all the day [one] fighting oppresses me.

en.L: Be gracious to me, God, for a mortal has trampled on me; all the day [one who is] fighting oppresses me.
en.B: God, show me grace, for people trample on me; all day long they fight me and press me hard.
en.R: God, be kind to me. People are stamping all over me. All day long they attack me and make my life hard.

decisions.choice: trampled on me: hounded me
decisions.reason: The verb (sha'af) can mean to trample or to pant after, as an animal chasing prey. It is repeated in verse 3.

decisions.choice: a mortal: a weak human being
decisions.reason: The word ('enosh) stresses human frailty (9:20-21). The psalm sets these attackers against God: in verse 5 they are "flesh", in verse 12 "human".

decisions.choice: people ... they
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of the attacker as one person standing for many (verse 3 says "many"); Balanced and Readable say "they".

source.text: שָׁאֲפ֣וּ שׁ֭וֹרְרַי כָּל־הַיּ֑וֹם כִּֽי־רַבִּ֨ים לֹחֲמִ֖ים לִ֣י מָרֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: My enemies have trampled all the day, for many [are] fighting against me, proudly.

en.L: My enemies have trampled [on me] all the day, for many [are] fighting against me proudly.
en.B: My enemies hound me all day long; many are fighting against me in their arrogance.
en.R: My enemies chase me all day long. So many proud people are fighting against me.

decisions.choice: proudly: from on high, arrogantly
decisions.reason: The word (marom) means height. It can describe the enemies as fighting from a height, that is, arrogantly; or it can be read as an address to God, "O Most High", as in 92:9.

decisions.choice: trampled: hounded
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

records.literal_gloss: [The] day I fear, I in you will trust.

en.L: [On the] day I am afraid, I — in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} I will trust.
en.B: On the day fear strikes, I will rely on {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.R: When I am scared, I will trust {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: I: my answer to fear
decisions.reason: The Hebrew adds "I" for emphasis: whatever the enemies do, this is what the psalmist will do.

decisions.choice: fear and trust together
decisions.reason: The psalmist does not deny that he is afraid; trust is his answer to fear. The next verse says that trust ends in not fearing.

source.text: בֵּאלֹהִים֮ אֲהַלֵּ֪ל דְּבָ֫ר֥וֹ בֵּאלֹהִ֣ים בָּ֭טַחְתִּי לֹ֣א אִירָ֑א מַה־יַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה בָשָׂ֣ר לִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: In God I praise his word; in God I have trusted; not I will fear; what can do flesh to me?

en.L: In God I praise {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word; in God I have trusted, I will not fear. What can flesh do to me?
en.B: With God I celebrate {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} promise; in God I have put my trust and will not be afraid. What can mere flesh do to me?
en.R: I praise God for what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has promised. I trust God, so fear has no hold on me. What can any human being do to me?

decisions.choice: his word: God's promise
decisions.reason: God's word here is what he has said he will do, his promise to protect (verse 10).

decisions.choice: In God I praise: with God's help, or praising God's word
alternatives: in God, whose word I praise
decisions.reason: "In God" may mean "with God's help" or "in God, whose word I praise". The sense is the same: the psalmist praises God for his word.

decisions.choice: flesh: a mortal, weak human
decisions.reason: Flesh is human life in its weakness (78:39; Isaiah 31:3). Against God, no human can finally harm him. Compare 118:6.

decisions.choice: a refrain
decisions.reason: Verses 11-12 repeat this verse with small changes.

decisions.choice: any human being
decisions.reason: Readable says what "flesh" means (m3).

source.text: כָּל־הַ֭יּוֹם דְּבָרַ֣י יְעַצֵּ֑בוּ עָלַ֖י כָּל־מַחְשְׁבֹתָ֣ם לָרָֽע׃

records.literal_gloss: All the day my words they twist; against me [are] all their thoughts for evil.

en.L: All the day they twist my words; all their plans [are] against me for harm.
en.B: All day long they twist what I say; every plan they make is for my harm.
en.R: All day long they change what I say to make it sound bad. They are always planning ways to hurt me.

decisions.choice: twist: distort
decisions.reason: The verb ('atsav) usually means to hurt or grieve. With "my words" it most likely means twisting what he says, or it may mean that they make his affairs go wrong.

decisions.choice: their thoughts: their plans
decisions.reason: The word (machashevet) means plans and schemes.

source.text: יָג֤וּרוּ׀יִצְפּ֗וֹנוּ הֵ֭מָּה עֲקֵבַ֣י יִשְׁמֹ֑רוּ כַּ֝אֲשֶׁ֗ר קִוּ֥וּ נַפְשִֽׁי׃

records.literal_gloss: They stir up strife, they hide, they — my heels they watch, as they have waited [for] my soul.

en.L: They stir up strife, they lie hidden; they watch my heels, as they have waited [for] my soul.
en.B: They band together and hide; they watch my every step, eager to take my life.
en.R: They get together and hide, waiting for me. They watch every step I take. They are waiting for the chance to kill me.

decisions.choice: they lie hidden: the form to be read
decisions.reason: The written text and the form to be read differ in one vowel letter of the verb "hide"; the meaning is the same. The words here follow the form to be read.

decisions.choice: stir up strife: gather to attack
decisions.reason: The verb (gur) may mean to stir up strife (59:4) or to gather as a band.

decisions.choice: watch my heels: follow my every step
decisions.reason: They keep close behind him, waiting for him to slip (17:11).

decisions.choice: my life (B); kill me (R)
decisions.reason: Nefesh here is life itself.

records.literal_gloss: For wickedness — escape for them? In anger peoples bring down, God.

en.L: For [their] wickedness, [is there] escape for them? In anger bring down [the] peoples, God.
en.B: Will they get away with such wickedness? God, in anger throw down the nations.
en.R: Should they escape after doing such evil? God, be angry with the nations and bring them down.

decisions.choice: escape for them?: a question expecting no
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is brief: "for wickedness, escape for them". Read as a question, it means they must not escape. Some read it as an ironic command, and some change one letter to read "weigh out to them", that is, "pay them back".

decisions.choice: the peoples: the nations hostile to God's people
decisions.reason: The enemies of the title were Philistines. The prayer widens to all the nations that oppose God (7:8-9; 59:6).

decisions.choice: the nations
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "nations" for the foreign peoples.

source.text: נֹדִי֮ סָפַ֪רְתָּ֫ה אָ֥תָּה שִׂ֣ימָה דִמְעָתִ֣י בְנֹאדֶ֑ךָ הֲ֝לֹ֗א בְּסִפְרָתֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: My wandering have counted you; put my tears in your skin bottle; [are they] not in your book?

en.L: My wanderings {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} have counted; put my tears in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} skin bottle; [are they] not in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} book?
en.B: You {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} have kept count of my wanderings; store my tears in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} flask. Are they not already in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} record?
en.R: You know every time I have had to run and hide. Save all my tears in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} jar. Have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} not written them down in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} book?

decisions.choice: my wandering: my life as a fugitive
decisions.reason: The word (nod) is restless wandering, like Cain's in the land of Nod (Genesis 4:12-16). It sounds like the word for the skin bottle (nod) in the next line.

decisions.choice: skin bottle: a container for keeping liquid
decisions.reason: A bottle made of animal skin held wine or water (Joshua 9:4). God is asked to keep every tear, so that none is forgotten.

decisions.choice: your book: God's record
decisions.reason: God keeps a record of his people and their lives (69:29; 139:16; Exodus 32:32).

decisions.choice: are they not?: a question expecting yes
decisions.reason: The question means that the tears are already recorded.

decisions.choice: You know every time I have had to run and hide
decisions.reason: Readable says what the wanderings were (m1).

source.text: אָ֥֨ז יָ֘שׁ֤וּבוּ אוֹיְבַ֣י אָ֭חוֹר בְּי֣וֹם אֶקְרָ֑א זֶה־יָ֝דַ֗עְתִּי כִּֽי־אֱלֹהִ֥ים לִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Then will turn my enemies backward on [the] day I call; this I know, that God [is] for me.

en.L: Then my enemies will turn backward on the day I call out; this I know: God [is] for me.
en.B: When I call for help, my enemies will retreat; this much I know, God is on my side.
en.R: When I call out to God, my enemies will run away. I know this for sure: God is on my side.

decisions.choice: this I know: what follows
decisions.reason: "This" points forward to what he knows: God is for him. It may also point back: the enemies' retreat shows that God is for him.

decisions.choice: God is for me: God is on my side
decisions.reason: Compare 118:6 and Romans 8:31, "If God is for us, who can be against us?"

decisions.choice: to God
decisions.reason: Readable says whom he calls.

source.text: בֵּֽ֭אלֹהִים אֲהַלֵּ֣ל דָּבָ֑ר בַּ֝יהוָ֗ה אֲהַלֵּ֥ל דָּבָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: In God I praise [the] word; in YHWH I praise [the] word,

en.L: In God I praise [the] word, in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} I praise [the] word,
en.B: In God, whose promise I celebrate, in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, whose promise I celebrate,
en.R: I praise God for what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has promised. I praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has said.

decisions.choice: the refrain, with the divine name
decisions.reason: Verses 11-12 repeat verse 5. This time the line is doubled, with "God" and then the divine name, which this psalm uses only here.

decisions.choice: the word: God's promise
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "word" without "his"; it is the same word of promise as in verse 5.

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: The sentence continues into verse 12, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

source.text: בֵּֽאלֹהִ֣ים בָּ֭טַחְתִּי לֹ֣א אִירָ֑א מַה־יַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה אָדָ֣ם לִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: in God I have trusted; not I will fear; what can do a human to me?

en.L: in God I have trusted, I will not fear. What can a human do to me?
en.B: in God I have put my trust; I will not fear. What can a mere human do to me?
en.R: I trust God, so I am not afraid. What can any person do to me?

decisions.choice: a human: a mere human being
decisions.reason: Verse 5 has "flesh"; this verse has "a human" ('adam). Both set human weakness against God.

decisions.choice: I have trusted, I will not fear
decisions.reason: Trust is settled (the past form), and so fear has no hold (the unfinished form).

source.text: עָלַ֣י אֱלֹהִ֣ים נְדָרֶ֑יךָ אֲשַׁלֵּ֖ם תּוֹדֹ֣ת לָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: On me, God, [are] your vows; I will pay thank offerings to you.

en.L: On me, God, [are] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} vows; I will repay thank offerings to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.B: God, I am bound by the vows I made to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; I will pay them with offerings of thanks to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.R: God, I will keep the promises I made to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. I will bring {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} offerings to thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: vows and thank offerings
decisions.reason: In trouble a person would vow to bring an offering when God answered; the thank offering (todah) kept the vow and gave thanks in public (Leviticus 7:12-16; 66:13-14).

decisions.choice: your vows: vows made to you
decisions.reason: "Your vows" are the vows the psalmist made to God, and they rest on him as a duty ("on me").

source.text: כִּ֤י הִצַּ֪לְתָּ נַפְשִׁ֡י מִמָּוֶת֮ הֲלֹ֥א רַגְלַ֗י מִ֫דֶּ֥חִי לְ֭הִֽתְהַלֵּךְ לִפְנֵ֣י אֱלֹהִ֑ים בְּ֝א֗וֹר הַֽחַיִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: For you have delivered my soul from death, [have you] not my feet from stumbling, to walk before God in [the] light of the living?

en.L: For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have rescued my soul from death, indeed my feet from stumbling, to walk about before God in the light of the living.
en.B: For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have rescued me from death and kept my feet from slipping, so that I can walk with God in the light of the living.
en.R: You have saved my life. You have kept me from falling. Now I can live my life with God and enjoy the light of being alive.

decisions.choice: not my feet?: a question expecting yes
alternatives: will you not keep my feet from stumbling?
decisions.reason: "Have you not ...?" is a strong way of saying "you have". Literal gives it as "indeed".

decisions.choice: walk before God: live in God's presence and service
decisions.reason: As God told Abraham, "Walk before me" (Genesis 17:1).

decisions.choice: the light of the living: life on earth
decisions.reason: Light belongs to life, darkness to death (Job 33:30).

decisions.choice: the same words in Psalm 116
decisions.reason: Psalm 116:8-9 has nearly the same lines.

decisions.choice: enjoy the light of being alive
alternatives: in the light of the living
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means (m3).
